query: Why is learning satisfaction low for certain groups, and which factors drive it?

per_column.name: pedagogy_adaptation_quality
per_column.rationale: A genuine axis distinguishing how well instruction adapted to the format, directly relevant to satisfaction drivers. Values are mostly warranted (ED-0002 'exemplary', ED-0003 'absent_or_negligible'), but ED-0001 marked 'adequate' despite the text describing lessons that 'don't click' and technical breakdown, a weakly supported read.

per_column.name: student_engagement_signal
per_column.rationale: Engagement is a core candidate driver of satisfaction and gives a useful grouping axis. Values track the text well (ED-0005 silent cameras -> disengaged, ED-0002 kids showing up -> active). ED-0001 'passive_compliant' is a defensible inference from 'I miss raising my hand'.

per_column.name: peer_social_interaction_loss
per_column.rationale: A distinct social dimension useful for explaining dissatisfaction. Well grounded where text mentions it (ED-0003 'zero peer interaction' -> severe). But ED-0001 'moderate' and ED-0002 'minimal' are asserted where the source says nothing about peer interaction, and ED-0005 'severe' conflates disengagement with peer loss.

per_column.name: teacher_feedback_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Feedback quality is a plausible satisfaction driver and a useful axis. However several values are unsupported: ED-0003 and ED-0005 lack any statement about feedback timing yet are labeled 'delayed_or_minimal', and ED-0004 'prompt_and_detailed' is not evidenced by the text.

per_column.name: subject_format_compatibility
per_column.rationale: Whether a subject suits remote delivery is a strong analytical axis and pairs with the existing subject column. Reads are mostly sound (algebra/whiteboard issues -> low; recorded history lectures -> high). Reasonable inferences overall.

per_column.name: instructional_design_mode
per_column.rationale: Delivery mode is a legitimate factor to segment on. ED-0004 'asynchronous_rich' (recorded, pause-at-own-pace) is well grounded. But 'synchronous_live_interactive' is over-applied to ED-0003 (platform logs out, self-done worksheet) and ED-0001 where the mode is not clearly synchronous, showing some unsupported specificity.

judge.rationale: All six added columns supply distinct, non-redundant analytical axes (pedagogy quality, engagement, peer loss, feedback, subject fit, delivery mode) that directly serve a query about drivers of low learning satisfaction; none are near-constant or trivial restatements. Groundedness is moderate: extractions are strong where the source explicitly discusses a theme, but several columns confidently assert categories (peer interaction, feedback timing, synchronous mode) for rows whose text is silent on those dimensions, rather than using an 'unknown' value. This over-confident inference is the main quality risk.
